classification.habitat: Cultivated gardens, hedges and warm tropical/subtropical settings
classification.distribution: Widely cultivated throughout India and other warm regions

identification.description: A much-branched ornamental shrub with glossy serrated leaves and large conspicuous flowers, commonly red but occurring in many cultivated colour forms.
identification.whole_plant: Evergreen branched shrub, often maintained as a hedge or garden plant.
identification.root: Fibrous to branched woody root system; not a primary field character.
identification.stem: Much-branched woody stems, green when young and becoming brown with age.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, ovate leaves with serrated margins and pointed tips.
identification.flower: Large showy axillary flowers with prominent staminal column; cultivated forms vary greatly in colour and petal arrangement.
identification.fruit: Cultivated Hibiscus rosa-sinensis commonly shows little or no fruiting; fruit characters are therefore not dependable for routine identification.
identification.seed: Seeds are not a reliable routine identification character in many cultivated forms.
identification.bark: Thin grey-brown bark on older branches.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Composition varies substantially with flower colour and cultivar. Avoid treating ornamental cultivar chemistry as identical across all Hibiscus material.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Hibiscus rosa-sinensis is primarily known as an ornamental species and is also represented in traditional medicinal literature. Evidence for specific clinical uses should be assessed preparation by preparation.
modern_information.safety_notes: Botanical cultivar variation is substantial; authenticate the material used for medicinal purposes.

student.quick_revision: Japa (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis) is a Malvaceae shrub with large axillary flowers; flower is the listed useful part in this project record.

teaching_points: Use the flower to demonstrate Malvaceae floral characters.
Discuss cultivar variation and why colour alone is not enough for authentication.
discussion_points: Ornamental cultivar diversity and medicinal-drug authentication
Traditional Keshya use versus modern evidence
practical_points: Label calyx, epicalyx if present, corolla, staminal column and stigma.
Compare leaf margin and phyllotaxy with another Malvaceae specimen.

doctor.quick_reference: Japa — Hibiscus rosa-sinensis L.; flower is the useful part in this project record, with traditional indications including Pradara and hair-related uses.
key_precautions: Authenticate the botanical material and cultivar.
Use authoritative references for formulation and dose decisions.
